learning_outcomes.text: Students should learn about joining processes and be able to evaluate them using examples. They will be able to identify causes of faulty joints.

Students who have successfully completed this module have deepened their knowledge of the heat influence of welding on the material. Furthermore, they have deepened knowledge of essential joining processes and can plan their use for specific thermal joining processes.

Students who have studied this module can assess the microstructures of joining connections and analyze the execution of a joining connection together with the hardness and strength properties. Students should also be able to evaluate the design of a construction with regard to chosen joining processes and their influence on the microstructure of the material. Suitable testing methods should be used to independently make a statement about the quality of the joining connection and, if necessary, identify potential for improvement.

Students who have successfully completed this module are able to process the results obtained from practical experiments in a team, discuss them taking into account the learned material and supplementary specialist literature, and present them in an appropriate form.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the historical development and economic importance of welding
Information on training as a welding engineer (prerequisites, activities, etc.)
Structure of welded joints (single-layer, multi-layer seams)
Temperature profile during welding in the weld metal and in the heat-affected zone (HAZ)
Evaluation of the microstructure in cohesive joining connections
Crack behavior in welded joints: cause and prevention of hot cracks and cold cracks
Classification of joining processes into main manufacturing group 4 according to DIN 8580: Brazing, Welding, Special processes
Areas of application and differentiation of various joining processes
Weldability according to DIN technical report ISO/TR581 (material suitability, manufacturing feasibility, design safety)
Arc types and droplet transfer including physical processes in the arc
Brazing of Cu and Cu alloys
Application examples and damage cases: fatigue fracture, terrace fracture, etc.
Pre-treatment and post-treatment, e.g., preheating, stress-relief annealing, carbon equivalent, solution annealing and aging
Methods of weld seam inspection and evaluation
Special processes such as submerged arc welding
Special autogenous processes Ti-welding and Al-welding

assessment_methods.method: Experimentelle Arbeit (Experimental work) including oral explanation as group work

assessment_rules: The overall grade is composed of a written exam (80%) and experimental work (20%). The experimental work includes an oral explanation as group work. The written exam is graded according to the valid study regulations. The experimental work is assessed based on the scope of the laboratory activities.
bibliography: U. Reisgen, L. Stein, Grundlagen der Fügetechnik, DVS-Verlag, 2016.
